justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies R-01 and R-02 via the Web Application (SPA) and BFF for customers, brokers, and adjusters. R-03 is directly fulfilled by the Feature Flag / Routing Service, Claim Management Core, and Anti-Corruption Layer managing incremental claim type migration.
justifications.performance_efficiency: R-05 is directly addressed by decoupling frontend reads from the 5-second mainframe response via the Cache / Read Model Store (In-Memory Cache Layer and Read Model Database Engine), BFF response caching, and asynchronous synchronization via Azure Service Bus and ETL Service.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability with the DB2 mainframe is handled by the Anti-Corruption Layer (Mainframe Adapter) and Data Synchronization / ETL Service, while Active Directory is integrated for SSO. However, compliance with the strict non-extendable nightly batch window (23:00-05:00) is not explicitly detailed.
justifications.usability: Both user groups (Customers/Brokers and Claims Adjusters) interact with the dedicated Web Application (SPA) with optimistic UI updates. However, combining external public submissions and internal adjuster workflows into a single SPA without dedicated role-specific interfaces is a minor usability concern.
justifications.reliability: Ensures R-04 via Outbox Table & Dispatcher in Claim Management Core, Outbox Pattern Handler in Service Bus, and Dead-Letter Queue Manager. R-06 is supported by the Circuit Breaker Manager and fallback-to-safe-default routing to switch back to the mainframe.
justifications.security: R-07 is fulfilled via the Authentication Client connecting to On-Premise Active Directory for SSO. Security & Middleware Handler enforces PII masking. However, external authentication/authorization for customers and brokers (who typically lack internal Active Directory accounts) is unspecified.
justifications.maintainability: Achieves high modularity through Clean Architecture, Ports & Adapters in the Domain Translator, Modular Domain Packages, and BFF pattern. R-06 rollback within one day is explicitly enabled by the Routing Controller, feature flags, and Cache Invalidation Publisher.
justifications.portability: The hybrid model respects the target environments (azure-westeurope and on-prem-mainframe) using containerized Azure App Services, ExpressRoute/VPN, and standardized protocols (REST, AMQP), keeping cloud-agnostic domain logic modular to accommodate the inexperienced cloud team.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture isolates slow mainframe reads by using CQRS with a denormalized Cache/Read Model Store and In-Memory Cache Layer populated asynchronously by the Data Synchronization/ETL Service, allowing BFF responses in under 2 seconds without synchronous mainframe calls.
sensitivity_points: Freshness of the read model depends on ETL and sync pipeline replication lag
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency in claim views traded for sub-second UI read performance

PERF-02.justification: Peak submission bursts are buffered through Azure Service Bus queues and the Outbox Pattern Handler in Claim Management Core, decoupling front-end ingestion from the mainframe. However, throttling logic to strictly protect the 23:00-05:00 batch window requires explicit scheduling controls.
sensitivity_points: Queue depth and message retention limits on Azure Service Bus during peak bursts
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission acceptance traded against immediate mainframe consistency confirmation

AVAIL-01.justification: The Outbox Table & Dispatcher paired with Azure Service Bus provides durable asynchronous queueing. Submissions continue operating in Azure during the batch window downtime and are forwarded to the Anti-Corruption Layer once the mainframe resumes processing.
sensitivity_points: Durability and capacity of cloud outbox tables during extended mainframe batch windows
tradeoffs: Deferred batch forwarding traded against immediate end-to-end claim registration

AVAIL-02.justification: The system applies transactional outbox messaging, dead-letter queues, and an Anti-Corruption Layer to prevent message loss. While partial failures are routed to DLQs and logged, the exact automated dual-direction state reconciliation process across DB2 and cloud is only partially detailed.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency key enforcement across hybrid network boundaries and mainframe legacy adapters
tradeoffs: Dead-letter isolation guarantees no data loss but requires operational manual intervention

MOD-01.justification: The Feature Flag / Routing Service with Consistent Hashing and circuit breaker fallback, combined with modular domain packages (Auto, Property) and an Anti-Corruption Layer, enables granular per-claim-type migration and rapid sub-day rollback without altering legacy schemas.
sensitivity_points: Centralized feature flag rule propagation latency across BFF and Core components
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual routing paths and ACL translation adds temporary operational complexity

MOD-02.justification: The modern Web Application (SPA) communicates strictly with the Backend-for-Frontend and Claim Management Core. Mainframe dependencies are fully encapsulated behind the Anti-Corruption Layer and ETL service, allowing the mainframe to be decommissioned with zero frontend UI modifications.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling depth of the BFF API contracts from legacy data attributes
tradeoffs: Investment in comprehensive ACL translation layers avoids future frontend rewriting costs

SEC-01.justification: The architecture provides Active Directory SSO, API gateway middleware, and Application Insights audit logging. However, it lacks an explicit domain authorization mechanism or attribute-based access control (ABAC) to enforce broker-customer tenancy isolation at the service or data level.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of fine-grained claims ownership authorization rules within BFF and Core
tradeoffs: Centralized authentication simplifies setup but misses granular tenant-level authorization logic

SEC-02.justification: Authentication is centralized on the on-premise Active Directory via SSO across the platform. Disabling the adjuster's account in Active Directory prevents new logins; however, achieving revocation within 15 minutes depends on token lifetime and active session revocation policies not explicitly defined.
sensitivity_points: Access token expiry windows and active session validation intervals in the BFF
tradeoffs: Short-lived tokens improve revocation speed but increase token refresh traffic across boundaries
